title: Learning Computational Structure for Sample-Efficient Prediction
abstract: arXiv:2610.28555v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Statistical learning in high dimensions suffers from the curse of dimensionality. Fortunately, many functions of practical interest are compositionally sparse, meaning they admit a composition of local functions, each depending on only a few variables, allowing sample complexity to depend on local arity rather than ambient dimension. Yet realizing this benefit requires exploiting hidden compositional structure, which theory does not establish for practical gradient-based training. We study this gap with CSFRBench, a controlled benchmark that hides the target's compositional computation during training but retains it for diagnosis, and find that dense networks and sparsity-based baselines leave much of that benefit unrealized. Inspired by the spatial organization of biological neural circuits, we introduce Learned Wiring (LeWi): each neuron has a learned low-dimensional embedding, only nearby neurons connect, and embeddings and weights

translated_title: 学习计算结构以实现样本高效的预测
translated_abstract: 高维统计学习饱受维数灾难的困扰。幸运的是，许多具有实际意义的函数是组合稀疏的，也就是说它们可以表示为若干局部函数的组合，每个局部函数仅依赖于少数几个变量，这使得样本复杂度取决于局部元数而非环境维度。然而，要真正获得这一好处，需要利用隐藏的组合结构，而现有理论并未针对实际基于梯度的训练方法确立这一点。我们通过 CSFRBench 来研究这一差距——这是一个受控基准，它在训练阶段隐藏目标函数的组合计算方式，但在诊断阶段保留该结构——并发现稠密网络以及基于稀疏性的基线方法都未能充分实现这一潜在收益。受生物神经回路空间组织方式的启发，我们提出了 Learned Wiring（LeWi，学习式布线）：每个神经元拥有一个可学习的低维嵌入，只有彼此邻近的神经元才会相互连接，并且嵌入与权重……（摘要原文在此处截断）
tldr: 受生物神经回路空间组织启发，该论文提出 CSFRBench 基准和 Learned Wiring（LeWi）方法——让每个神经元学习低维嵌入并仅与邻近神经元连接——以显式利用函数的组合稀疏结构，从而显著提升高维预测的样本效率。
en_tdlr: Inspired by the spatial organization of biological neural circuits, this paper proposes the CSFRBench benchmark and Learned Wiring (LeWi), where each neuron learns a low-dimensional embedding and connects only to nearby neurons, explicitly exploiting compositional sparsity to achieve sample-efficient prediction in high dimensions.
